# Proposal: Greeting module boundary contract

## Problem

`src/greeting.mjs` currently exports `greet` only. The configured runtime validators require a `FAREWELL` string export with value `bye`, and the architecture validator requires the greeting module's exact named-export surface to be `FAREWELL` and `greet`. There is no usage module that re-exports the farewell value.

## Desired outcome

Add `FAREWELL` to the canonical greeting module and add a separate usage module that re-exports it. Preserve the existing `greet(name)` behavior and keep `src/greeting.mjs`'s public named exports exactly `FAREWELL` and `greet`.

## Scope

- Export `FAREWELL` from `src/greeting.mjs` as the string `bye`.
- Add `src/usage.mjs`, which re-exports `FAREWELL` from `src/greeting.mjs`.
- Keep the dependency one-way: the usage module depends on the greeting module.
- Keep the greeting module's exact named-export surface as `FAREWELL` and `greet`.

## Non-goals

- Do not change the greeting text or `greet(name)` behavior.
- Do not add other exports to either module or change validator configuration.
- Do not introduce a `src/format.mjs` module; its presence activates existing architecture cycle checks.

## Observable behavior

This change adds an externally observable named export to `src/greeting.mjs` and a new import path at `src/usage.mjs`. It is a behavior-visible API change, so this proposal includes a delta spec.
artifacts.design:
# Design: Greeting module boundary contract

## Boundaries and approach

`src/greeting.mjs` remains the canonical public greeting module. Declare `FAREWELL` there as `export const FAREWELL = "bye"` and retain the existing `greet` function. The module must expose no other exports: `scripts/contract.mjs` checks its runtime keys, and `scripts/architecture.mjs` checks the declared export names.

Add `src/usage.mjs` with a direct re-export of `FAREWELL` from `./greeting.mjs`. Keep the dependency one-way so the new module cannot introduce a cycle. The chosen path avoids `src/format.mjs`, whose presence activates conditional cycle checks in `scripts/architecture.mjs`.

## Compatibility and risks

Existing consumers of `greet` retain the same behavior. Consumers gain the `FAREWELL` named export with value `bye`. The exact-key contract means no helper or default export can be added to `src/greeting.mjs`.

## Validation evidence

Run `node scripts/validate.mjs` and `node scripts/contract.mjs`, the explicit acceptance commands. Also run `node scripts/architecture.mjs` to verify the statically checked exact export surface and module-boundary rules.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Greeting exports FAREWELL and preserves its exact export surface

The greeting module SHALL export the string constant `FAREWELL` with value `bye`, preserve the existing `greet` behavior, and expose exactly the named exports `FAREWELL` and `greet`.

#### Scenario: Consumer imports the greeting contract

- GIVEN a consumer imports `src/greeting.mjs`
- WHEN the consumer reads its exported values and keys
- THEN `FAREWELL` is the string `bye`
- AND `greet("AEH")` returns `Hello, AEH!`
- AND the module's named export keys are exactly `FAREWELL` and `greet`

### Requirement: Usage module re-exports FAREWELL

The usage module at `src/usage.mjs` SHALL re-export `FAREWELL` from `src/greeting.mjs` as its only named export.

#### Scenario: Consumer imports the usage module

- GIVEN a consumer imports `src/usage.mjs`
- WHEN the consumer reads `FAREWELL`
- THEN its value is `bye`
- AND the usage module exposes no other named export

payload.summary: Bounded discovery for the greeting module-boundary change: src/greeting.mjs currently exports only greet, while all three validators already demand an exact surface of {greet, FAREWELL} with FAREWELL === "bye". Baseline is therefore red; the change must add `export const FAREWELL = "bye"` inside src/greeting.mjs itself (architecture.mjs counts only `export const|function|class NAME` declarations, so re-export syntax is invisible) plus a separate one-way usage module that re-exports FAREWELL. The usage module must not be named src/format.mjs (that would activate the architecture cycle rule) and greeting.mjs must not gain any additional exports (contract.mjs rejects unexpected keys).

artifacts.proposal:
# Proposal: Greeting module boundary contract

## Problem

`src/greeting.mjs` currently exports `greet` only. The configured runtime validators require a `FAREWELL` string export with value `bye`, and the architecture validator requires the greeting module's exact named-export surface to be `FAREWELL` and `greet`. There is no usage module that re-exports the farewell value.

## Desired outcome

Add `FAREWELL` to the canonical greeting module and add a separate usage module that re-exports it. Preserve the existing `greet(name)` behavior and keep `src/greeting.mjs`'s public named exports exactly `FAREWELL` and `greet`.

## Scope

- Export `FAREWELL` from `src/greeting.mjs` as the string `bye`.
- Add `src/usage.mjs`, which re-exports `FAREWELL` from `src/greeting.mjs`.
- Keep the dependency one-way: the usage module depends on the greeting module.
- Keep the greeting module's exact named-export surface as `FAREWELL` and `greet`.

## Non-goals

- Do not change the greeting text or `greet(name)` behavior.
- Do not add other exports to either module or change validator configuration.
- Do not introduce a `src/format.mjs` module; its presence activates existing architecture cycle checks.

## Observable behavior

This change adds an externally observable named export to `src/greeting.mjs` and a new import path at `src/usage.mjs`. It is a behavior-visible API change, so this proposal includes a delta spec.
artifacts.design:
# Design: Greeting module boundary contract

## Boundaries and approach

`src/greeting.mjs` remains the canonical public greeting module. Declare `FAREWELL` there as `export const FAREWELL = "bye"` and retain the existing `greet` function. The module must expose no other exports: `scripts/contract.mjs` checks its runtime keys, and `scripts/architecture.mjs` checks the declared export names.

Add `src/usage.mjs` with a direct re-export of `FAREWELL` from `./greeting.mjs`. Keep the dependency one-way so the new module cannot introduce a cycle. The chosen path avoids `src/format.mjs`, whose presence activates conditional cycle checks in `scripts/architecture.mjs`.

## Compatibility and risks

Existing consumers of `greet` retain the same behavior. Consumers gain the `FAREWELL` named export with value `bye`. The exact-key contract means no helper or default export can be added to `src/greeting.mjs`.

## Validation evidence

Run `node scripts/validate.mjs` and `node scripts/contract.mjs`, the explicit acceptance commands. Also run `node scripts/architecture.mjs` to verify the statically checked exact export surface and module-boundary rules.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Greeting exports FAREWELL and preserves its exact export surface

The greeting module SHALL export the string constant `FAREWELL` with value `bye`, preserve the existing `greet` behavior, and expose exactly the named exports `FAREWELL` and `greet`.

#### Scenario: Consumer imports the greeting contract

- GIVEN a consumer imports `src/greeting.mjs`
- WHEN the consumer reads its exported values and keys
- THEN `FAREWELL` is the string `bye`
- AND `greet("AEH")` returns `Hello, AEH!`
- AND the module's named export keys are exactly `FAREWELL` and `greet`

### Requirement: Usage module re-exports FAREWELL

The usage module at `src/usage.mjs` SHALL re-export `FAREWELL` from `src/greeting.mjs` as its only named export.

#### Scenario: Consumer imports the usage module

- GIVEN a consumer imports `src/usage.mjs`
- WHEN the consumer reads `FAREWELL`
- THEN its value is `bye`
- AND the usage module exposes no other named export
